# Documenting the dynamic slang of Dhaka in a dictionary

Mushfiqur Rahman

Cover of the the 'Bangla Slang Dictionary'Collected

Language is not static. It flows, bends and reshapes itself with time, much like a river that absorbs new streams while leaving some old channels behind. The Bangla Slang Dictionary, compiled under the initiative of Amin Rahman and his collaborators, is a valuable attempt to document one such living stream of language: the rich and colourful slang of Dhaka and its surrounding regions.

At first glance, slang may appear to belong to the margins of language. It is often informal, sometimes playful, occasionally irreverent. Yet history shows that many expressions once dismissed as slang eventually become part of accepted language. Conversely, when formal expressions fade from everyday speech, slang frequently takes their place in daily communication. For that reason, a dictionary devoted to slang is not merely a catalogue of colourful phrases; it is an important linguistic record of how people actually speak.

This dictionary serves a particularly useful role in bridging two linguistic communities. On one side stand the traditionalists who are accustomed to standard Bengali and may find certain colloquial expressions unfamiliar or puzzling. On the other side is a younger or more locally embedded community of speakers who naturally employ slang in everyday interaction. By presenting standard Bengali words alongside their slang equivalents, the dictionary allows readers from both groups to better understand each other.

As someone who grew up in a village on the outskirts of Dhaka but has lived outside Bangladesh for more than five decades, I found my own experience with this dictionary both surprising and enlightening. While browsing through its pages, I discovered that many of the slang words sounded unfamiliar, even foreign, to my ears. Part of this is no doubt due to the simple fact that I have not been immersed in everyday speech in Bangladesh for many years. In other cases, the expressions themselves appear to be relatively new, coined long after my early years in the country.

For me, therefore, this dictionary became more than just a reference book. It opened a window into how my mother tongue has continued to evolve during my long absence. It reminded me that language never stands still; it moves forward with each generation, absorbing new influences, new humour, and new modes of expression.

In that sense, the dictionary performs another valuable function: it reconnects those of us living abroad with the linguistic pulse of contemporary Bangladesh. By providing a clear guide to these expressions and their meanings, it equips readers like me with a practical tool. I have little doubt that during my next visit to Bangladesh, this knowledge will help me communicate more comfortably and confidently with the younger generation.

The editors also deserve credit for the care with which the material has been assembled. The inclusion of phonetic transcription and careful categorisation adds scholarly value to the work and makes it useful not only for casual readers but also for those interested in linguistics and dialect studies.

Slang, by its very nature, is dynamic. New words will inevitably emerge, while others will fade away. But that is precisely why works such as this are important. They capture a living snapshot of language at a particular moment in time.

The cover of the book deserves a brief mention as well. It features a striking image of a winding river, an apt visual metaphor for language itself — constantly flowing, branching and reshaping its course over time. Superimposed on this landscape is a short poem written entirely in Bangla slang. The playful lines celebrate the ease and confidence with which the younger generation uses slang in everyday speech. In a sense, the poem serves as a fitting prelude to the dictionary itself, reminding readers that slang is not merely informal speech but an important and vibrant layer of a living language.

Amin Rahman and his colleagues deserve appreciation for undertaking this ambitious project. By documenting the slang of Dhaka and its surrounding regions, they have preserved an important layer of Bengali linguistic culture — one that reflects the humour, vitality and everyday life of the people who speak it.

_**\\* Mushfiqur Rahman is a retired telecommunications specialist based in Melbourne, Australia. He can be reached at Rahman.mushfiq@gmail.com.**_

Want to learn a couple of slang words in Bengali? If you’re here, I’m sure you do. That’s why in this article, I will share with you some words that are commonly used every day in Bengali slang. To your surprise, the Bengali spoken in West Bengal, Kolkata, and many other places reflects plenty of cultural differences. However, the language is also very colorful and often humorous when it comes to slang.

These are not just random words with different meanings—they offer insight into the humor, wit, and emotions of Bengali people. So, if you want to talk like a native, let’s explore ten everyday **Bengali slang words** that will shake up your funny bone.

## 10 Bengali Slang Words

It is really interesting how slang is a fundamental part of any language because it adds humor and emotions to it.

Here are ten **Bengali slang words** that are commonly used in daily conversation:

### 1\. Are You Crazy – Pagol Na Matha Kharap? (পাগল না মাথা খারাপ?)

This Bengali slang word carries a humorous tone and is not meant to be taken seriously but rather as a rhetorical question. It is mainly used between friends or those who know each other well if one has done something that surprises the other.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I’m having 3 biryanis, and you’re eating 5? Are you crazy? | আমি ৩টা বিরিয়ানি খাবো, তুমি ৫টা খাচ্ছো? পাগল না মাথা খারাপ? | Ami 3 ta biryani khabo, tumi 5 ta khachcho? Pagol na matha kharap? |

### 2\. Torn Apart – Fata Fati (ফাটাফাটি)

This term expresses that something is awesome or great. Although its direct meaning is ‘torn apart,’ it is often used positively and enthusiastically. It can also mean praise or describe something that leaves a powerful impression.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| That concert was absolutely awesome! | সেই কনসার্টটা ফাটাফাটি ছিলো! | Sei concert ta fata fati chhilo! |

### **3\.** Umbrella Head – Chhatar Matha (ছাতার মাথা)

This **Bengali slang word** is commonly used to refer to a person who always escapes or prefers not to deal with issues or to ‘duck’ them. The expression has a humorous slant, indicating that the head of the person in question offers them protection in the shape of an umbrella from responsibility or adversity. It can also mean a person who is always in the middle of things without getting his or her hands dirty or taking any ownership of it.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oh dear, you’ve become such an umbrella head! | আরে বাবা, তুমি একদম ছাতার মাথা হয়ে গেছো! | Are baba, tumi ekdom chhatar matha hoye gecho! |

### 4\. Know-It-All – Pond Paka (পন্ড পাকা)

This term describes someone who acts like a know-it-all. It is usually used to refer to a person who is arrogant or condescending about something they know or think they know when in fact, they may not.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| You’ve become such a know-it-all! Learn a few things first. | তুই একদম পন্ড পাকা হয়ে গেছিস! কিছু শিখে নে আগে। | Tui ekdom pond paka hoyechhish! Kichhu shikhe ne age. |

### 5 **.** Frog’s Head – Baing Er Matha (ব্যাঙের মাথা)

This **Bengali slang word** suggests that the person is rigid or cannot take another person’s advice, just as a frog will not hop off its position waiting for a food insect to come closer. It can be used in a joking manner or rhetorically when a person becomes stiff-necked and unwilling to accept the other’s point of view or change his/her mind.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Don’t make a fuss out of everything! | সব কিছু নিয়ে ব্যাঙের মাথা বানাবি না! | Shab kichhu niye baing er matha banabi na! |

### **6\.** Oh My God! – Uri Baba! (উরি বাবা!)

This term is similar to the English expression ‘Oh my God!’ It is used when someone is surprised, astonished, or even cannot believe something. It is most commonly used when something surprising, shocking, or impressive occurs. It is used not only in informal conversations but also in other critical situations.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oh my God! Such a big fish! | উরি বাবা! এতো বড়ো মাছ! | Uri baba! Eto boro maachh! |

### 7\. Over- Smart – Paka (পাকা)

This slang term literally describes a person who is over-smart or overbearing in a way that is not liked. It refers to a person who has an attitude of a know-it-all or a conceited person, especially given his age or experience. A young person trying to act overly mature or knowledgeable might be called _Paka_.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| You’ve become so over-smart! | তুই একদম পাকা হয়ে গেছিস! | Tui ekdom paka hoye gechhish! |

![Impressed Man](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20450'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

### 8\. Fantastic / Stylish / Impressive – Ghyama (ঘ্যামা)

_Ghyama_(ঘ্যামা) is a slang used in the Bengali language to express something or someone is fantastic, stylish, or impressive. It is often used to pay someone or something a [compliment in Bengali](https://ling-app.com/bn/compliments-in-bengali/), especially when one or the other positively attracts attention. It is used most commonly in casual settings to express enthusiasm or cheer about something popular or ‘hip.’

**Example**:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your new shoes look fantastic! | তোর নতুন জুতো ঘ্যামা লাগছে! | Tor notun juto ghyama lagche! |

### 9\. Knowledgeable – Gyaani (জ্ঞানী)

_Gyaani_(জ্ঞানী) describes a well-educated or profoundly knowledgeable person. It is mostly said positively, but may also be used ironically or jokingly if the person being addressed is thought to be arrogant or a know-it-all.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronunciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oh, Mr. Genius, your advice is indispensable, isn’t it? | আর জ্ঞানী, তোর অ্যাডভাইস না দিলে চলছে না। | Are gyaani, tor advice na dile cholchhe na. |

### 10\. Don’t Worry – Tension Niyo Na (টেনশন নিও না)

It is a **Bengali slang word** typically used when people tend to be overly worried, or their brains get overwhelmed by a particular issue. People use this word with their friends, relatives, or anyone they know to reassure them or to tell them not to stress too much about something.

Example:

| English | Bengali | Pronounciation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Don’t worry, everything will be fine. | তুই টেনশন নিও না, সব ঠিক হবে। | Tui tension niyo na, shob thik hobe. |

## Tips For Using Bengali Slang

Learning **Bengali slang words** is a great way to expand and diversify your [Bengali vocabulary](https://www.ling-app.com/bn/bengali-vocabulary/) and build relationships with native speakers. However, you need to be careful, as using slang incorrectly can lead to misunderstandings or even offend someone.

- Understand the Context: Some Bengali words are funny to pronounce, but they can have a bad meaning, so be careful in order to avoid using them incorrectly.

- Learn from Native Speakers: The best way to understand the tone and emotion of the words is to talk to Bengali friends so you can understand how to use them properly.

- Practice makes perfect. Applications like the [Ling app](https://www.ling-app.com/) can help you practice and familiarize yourself with Bengali vocabulary and culture so that you can use slang words and other phrases with ease.

## How Do You Say “Slang” In Bengali?

In Bengali, the term “slang” is called _অপবাদ_ (Apababad), pronounced as _apa-babad_.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Bengali Slang Words

### 1\. What Are The Slangs Used In Kolkata?

In Kolkata, popular slang words include “ _hebby_,” which means “awesome,” “ _Ami toh bindaas_,” which translates to “I’m carefree,” and “ _Jhol,”_ which refers to a mess or chaos and is commonly used in casual conversations.

### 2\. What Is The Meaning Of Paka Buri?

The literal meaning is “ripe old woman.” It’s used humorously or sarcastically to describe an older woman who is perceived as overly wise, sometimes exaggeratedly or annoyingly. It implies that the person is overly experienced or knows everything.

### 3\. Do Older People Use Slang Words In Bengali?

Yes, older people in Bengali-speaking communities do use Bengali slang words, although it tends to vary depending on the individual and their generation. Older generations often have their own set of slang or colloquial expressions that may be different from what younger people use. These slang words are typically influenced by the socio-cultural environment of their time and may include terms that were popular in their youth or have evolved over the years.

## Wrapping Up

**Bengali slang words** such as _chhatar matha_ and _hebby_ are expressions that add a fun and expressive touch to everyday conversations. They reflect the [Bengali culture](https://www.britannica.com/place/West-Bengal), humor, and wit of Bengali-speaking people. As you continue to learn and use these Bengali slang words, remember to pay attention to the context and tone to avoid misunderstandings.

Happy learning!

# আসেন সাংসদের ৮৭ গালাগালির লিস্ট খান দেখি

## ২১ শে মে, ২০১৬ রাত ১০:১৮

বাংলাদেশের হিন্দুরা অনেকেই এখন "জল" কে "পানি" আর আদাব/নমস্কারের পরিবর্তে টেলিফোন তুলে আচ্ছালামু-আলাইকুম বলে। তবে, কোন হিন্দু "পাক" কিংবা "নাপাক" শব্দ এখনও লব্জ (কথায় কথায় বলা) করে নাই বলিয়া আমার শতভাগ বিশ্বাস আছে। বাংলাদেশে এখন হিন্দুরা যেমন পাল্টাচ্ছে, মুসলিমরাও পাল্টাচ্ছে। খোদাও এখন আল্লাহ্‌ হয়েছে। তাই পাক/নাপাকের ঘোলায় পরে যাত্রীসহ নৌকা টলটলায়মান। যেকোন সময় তলিয়ে যেতে পারে এইরকম ভাব। তাতে আর বিচিত্র কি? আল্লাহ্‌র ইচ্ছা ছাড়াতো আর গাছের পাতাও নড়েনা। তাই অটোম্যান ওসমান পরিবার ও হেফাজতে-জামায়াত যাঁহা যাঁহা করিবে তাহা আল্লাহ্‌র ইচ্ছায়ই হইবে। নারায়ণগঞ্জে ওসমান পরিবারের ইঙ্গিত ছাড়া কোন কিছু নড়েচড়ে না। ফোনালাপের ন্যায় তাঁরা ছাড়া আর কেউ ......মারার নেই! হেফাজতের গানের ভিডিও ও বাবুনগরীর ভিডিও আর ফোনালাপের সংলাপ একই সুরে গাঁথা, তা নিয়ে আপনার আমার কেন মাথা ব্যাথা। মদিনা সনদ অলরেডি বাস্তবায়ন হয়েছে, এখন শুধু শরিয়া আইন চালু হওয়ার অপেক্ষায় আছে। চাপাতি রেডি আছে, শুধু অটোম্যান আল্লাহু আকবর বলে রাস্তায় বের হওয়া বাকি। তখন আমরা আপনারা মুইত্তা দিলে ভাইস্যা যামু!

সেলিম ওসমান এবং সাংবাদিক নাফিজের সেই আলোচিত পুরো অডিওটি শুনলাম। অডিওটির মোট সময় ১৯ মিনিট ৪৯ সেকেন্ড। সেখানে এই সাংসদ সব মিলিয়ে ৮৭ টা গাল দিয়েছেন। তিনি যে যে গালি যতবার দিয়েছেন সেগুলোর একটা লিস্ট বানিয়েছি। এই স্ট্যাটাসটি ১৮+। অশ্লীল শব্দে যারা আহত হন কিংবা মন খারাপ করেন তাঁদেরকে সবিনয়ে অনুরোধ করছি গালাগালির লিস্ট টি না পড়বার জন্য। তবে আগ্রহীরা নীচে গিয়ে গালাগালের পরিসংখ্যানটি এক নজরে দেখে নিতে পারেন।

# গালি

গালি[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Profanity.svg/500px-Profanity.svg.png?utm_source=bn.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%9A%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0:Profanity.svg) [কার্টুন](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%A8 "কার্টুন") ও [কমিক্সে](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B8 "কমিক্স") প্রায়শই গালিকে অন্য চিহ্ন দিয়ে প্রতিস্থাপিত করে ব্যবহার করা হয় ( [মর্ট ওয়াকার](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%9F_%E0%A6%93%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0?action=edit&redlink=1 "মর্ট ওয়াকার") অঙ্কিত কার্টুন)।

**গালি** বা কথ্যভাষায় **গাইল** হল এক ধরনের ভাষাভিত্তিক শব্দ, শব্দগুচ্ছ বা বাক্যাংশ যা মূলত কটূক্তি এবং যা অন্য কোনো ব্যক্তির নিন্দাবাদ, অপমান বা অভিসম্পাতের উদ্দেশ্যে ব্যবহৃত হয়ে থাকে। যখন পরস্পরের মধ্যে গালি বিনিময় হয় তখন একে **গালিগালাজ** বলে উল্লেখ করা হয়। গালির জন্য সাধারণ শব্দ, **অকথ্য শব্দ** এবং **অশ্লীল শব্দ** — এই ত্রিবিধ শব্দাবলী ব্যবহৃত হয়ে থাকে।

কিছু গালি সাধারণভাবে প্রচলিত; আবার কিছু গালি নির্দিষ্ট গোষ্ঠীর সদস্যদের মধ্যে প্রচলিত যা কোনো কোনো ক্ষেত্রে সেই গোষ্ঠীর বৈশিষ্ট্য ফুটিয়ে তোলে। একই ভাষাভাষী মানুষের মধ্যে সংস্কৃতিভেদে গালির উদ্দেশ্য ও ব্যবহার ভিন্ন হতে পারে। গালি যেমন ব্যক্তিকে হেয় করার জন্য প্রয়োগ করা হয়, তেমনি গোষ্ঠীগত অবমাননার উদ্দেশ্যেও গালি প্রদান করা হয়ে থাকে। মানুষ নয় এমন প্রাণী বা বস্তুকেও গালি দেয়া হয়ে থাকে। গালির তীব্রতা বৃদ্ধির জন্য সাধারণ শব্দের পরিবর্তে অশালীন বা অশ্লীল শব্দের প্রয়োগ মানুষের একটি স্বাভাবিক প্রবণতা।[\[১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8-1)[\[২\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC-2)[\[৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%96-3)

গালি আর অকথ্যভাষা অভিন্ন নয়। উদ্দেশ্যের দিক থেকে গালি একধরনের সমালোচনা যা নির্দোষ থেকে আক্রমণাত্মক হতে পারে। গালমন্দ করে মানুষ নিজের ক্ষোভ করে অন্য দিকে ঘৃণাপ্রকাশেল সুখ লাভ করে থাকে।

## ব্যুৎপত্তি

ভাষাবিদ ও অভিধানবিদ বেন জিমার বলেন, "ঐতিহাসিক দিক থেকে গালিকে শনাক্ত করা বেশ কঠিন।"[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4) এর কারণ হিসেবে তিনি বলেন গালি লেখ্যরূপ পাবার অনেক আগে থেকে কথ্যরূপে ব্যবহৃত হয়ে থাকে। এর মধ্যে ঐ শব্দের অর্থ পরিবর্তিত হতে পারে এবং নতুন শব্দ প্রবেশ করতে পারে। এর ফলে গোটা প্রক্রিয়াই জটিল হয়ে পড়ে।[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4) অশ্লীল শব্দার্থে এর ইংরেজি "প্রোফ্যানিটি", যা লাতিন _প্রোফ্যানাস_ ( _profanus_) থেকে এসেছে, যার অর্থ "মন্দিরের পূর্বে (বাইরে)"।[\[৫\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-ProfanityWord-5) এখানে _প্রো_ অর্থ বাইরে আর _ফ্যানাম_ অর্থ মন্দির। প্রোফ্যান বলতে পবিত্রতার অভাব বুঝানো হতো, অন্তত ১৪৫০-এর দিকে। গালি শব্দের অন্যতম (এবং কম নেতিবাচক) ইংরেজি _স্ল্যাং_ শব্দের ব্যবহার দেখতে পাওয়া যায় ১৭৫৬ সালের দিকে। তখন এই শব্দের অর্থ ছিল "নিম্ন" বা "অসম্মানীয়" লোকের ব্যবহৃত শব্দ। উনবিংশ শতকের গোড়ার দিক থেকে স্ল্যাং আর তথাকথিত নিম্নশ্রেণীর লোকের ভাষা হিসেবে সীমাবদ্ধ ছিল না, যদিও এর অর্থগত দিক থেকে ব্যবহার শিক্ষিত বক্তব্যের আওতার বাইরে ছিল।[\[৬\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-oed-6) এই শব্দের ব্যুৎপত্তি নিশ্চিতভাবে জানা যায় না। জোনাথন গ্রিন বলেন, স্ল্যাং শব্দের অর্থ স্ক্যান্ডিনেভিয় শব্দ "স্লেঙ্গেনাম" থেকে আসার সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে, যে শব্দটি _স্লিং_ (ছুঁড়ে দেয়া) শব্দেরও স্রষ্টা। তিনি বলেন স্ল্যাং ছুঁড়ে দেয়া ভাষার অংশ, নিজের বক্তব্য তুলে ধরার দ্রুত ও সৎ উপায়।"[\[৭\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-etymonline-7)[\[৮\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-BriefHistory-8) গ্রিনের মতে প্রাথমিকভাবে গালি ব্যবহৃত হতো অপরাধীদের মধ্যে, তাদের নিজেদের আলোচনা কর্তৃপক্ষের থেকে আড়াল করার জন্য।[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4) বাংলা গালি শব্দটি এসেছে [সংস্কৃত](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%83%E0%A6%A4_%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B7%E0%A6%BE "সংস্কৃত ভাষা") √গাল্ \+ ই-তু. আ. থেকে।

## মনস্তত্ত্ব ও কারণ

হাঁটার পথে হোঁচট খেলে বা ব্যথা পেলে অনেক ক্ষেত্রে সহজাত প্রবৃত্তির মত সহজভাবে অশ্লীল শব্দ বা গালি চলে আসে।[\[১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8-1)[\[৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%96-3) কখনো কখনো নির্দিষ্ট গোষ্ঠীর ব্যবহৃত গালি প্রমাণ করে যে বাকিরা ঐ গোষ্ঠীর বাইরে।[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4)[\[৯\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A3-9) ড. এমা বার্ন তার লেখা _সোয়ারিং ইজ গুড ফর ইউ_ শীর্ষক বইয়ে বলেন, গালি হচ্ছে এমন এক ধরনের ভাষা যা আমরা চমকে গেলে বা স্তম্ভিত হলে বা উৎফুল্ল হলে পরে ব্যবহার করি; অথবা মজা করার জন্য বা কারো প্রতি আক্রমণাত্মক হবার জন্যও ব্যবহার করি। তবে এটা এমন একটা সাংস্কৃতিক ব্যাপার যা কেবল একটি জনগোষ্ঠী, ভাষা, সমাজ, দেশ বা ধর্মের মধ্যেই অর্থপূর্ণ হতে পারে।" অনেক সময়েই বিশেষ সংস্কৃতিতে আপাত নিষিদ্ধ বা ট্যাবু জিনিস থেকে গালি সৃষ্টি হয়। এক্ষেত্রে প্রাণীর নাম, শারীরিক সমস্যাও গালি হিসেবে ব্যবহৃত হয়। অনেক ক্ষেত্রেই এর প্রধান লক্ষ্য মানসিক আঘাত সৃষ্টি করা। কিল বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের মনোবিজ্ঞানের জ্যেষ্ঠ প্রভাষক ড. রিচার্ড স্টিভেন্সের _স্ল্যাং ল্যাবরেটরি_ নামক গবেষণাকেন্দ্রে পরিচালিত গবেষণায় দেখা যায় কিছু ক্ষেত্রে গালি দীর্ঘসময় একই যন্ত্রণা সহ্য করতে সহায়ক হয়। এর কারণ গালির সাথে আবেগের সংযোগ থাকে, আর তার প্রতিক্রিয়া সৃষ্টি হয়। গালি দেয়ার সময় হৃদপিণ্ডের গতিও বেড়ে যায়। মানসিক চাপের মধ্যে বা মানসিকভাবে আঘাতপ্রাপ্ত হওয়ার সময় গালি দিলে এমন প্রতিক্রিয়া সৃষ্টি হতে পারে, যা পূর্বের ব্যথার অনুভূতিকে কিছুটা লাঘব করে দেয়। এই বিশেষ ক্রিয়ার নাম স্ট্রেস-ইন্ডিউউসড অ্যানালজেসিয়া। সংস্কৃতিভেদে গালি অনেক বৈচিত্র্যময় হয়ে থাকে। কখনো পূর্বাপর প্রজন্মকে নির্দেশ করে গালি দেয়া হয়। ম্যান্ডারিন ভাষার কিছু গালি ১৮ প্রজন্মের আগের পূর্বপুরুষকেও সংযুক্ত করে।[\[৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%96-3)

যুক্তরাষ্ট্রভিত্তিক [অ্যাসোসিয়েশন অব সাইকোলজিক্যাল সায়েন্স](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%85%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%A8_%E0%A6%85%E0%A6%AC_%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%87%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2_%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B8?action=edit&redlink=1 "অ্যাসোসিয়েশন অব সাইকোলজিক্যাল সায়েন্স") জার্নালে প্রকাশিত _দ্য ইউটিলিটি অ্যান্ড ইউবিকুইটি অব ট্যাবু ওয়ার্ডস_ শীর্ষক গবেষণাপ্রবন্ধে মনোবিদ টিমোথি জে গালি দেয়াটাকে গাড়ির হর্ন বাজানোর সাথে তুলনা করেন। অন্যের প্রতিক্রিয়া দেখার জন্যও গালির ব্যবহার হতে পারে বলে তিনি মতপ্রকাশ করেন, যেন অন্যের চরিত্রের ভিন্নরূপ আবিষ্কার করা যায়। "রাগ, হতাশা, আনন্দ বা বিস্ময়—এমন আবেগের তীব্রতা বোঝানোর জন্য মানুষ এ ধরনের শব্দ ব্যবহার করে থাকে" বলেও তিনি জানান।[\[১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8-1)[\[১০\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9C%E0%A7%87-10)

## সাহিত্যে গালির ব্যবহার

সাহিত্যে বরাবরই গালির ব্যবহার হয়ে আসছে। [উইলিয়াম শেক্সপিয়ার](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%87%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AE_%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0 "উইলিয়াম শেক্সপিয়ার") তার লেখায় গালির (স্ল্যাং) ব্যবহার করেছেন।[\[১১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%99%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE-11)

## ভাষাগত লিঙ্গবৈষম্য

ভাষাবিদ ও সমাজতাত্ত্বিকেরা ভাষার মাধ্যমে লিঙ্গবৈষম্যের কথা তুলে ধরেন।[\[১২\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8-12)[\[১৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%95-13) _ডিকশনারি অব আমেরিকান স্ল্যাং_ তৈরির সময় ১৯৭০-এর দশকে ফ্লেক্সনার দেখেন যে "অধিকাংশ মার্কিন গালি তৈরি ও ব্যবহৃত হচ্ছে পুরুষের দ্বারা।"[\[১৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%AB%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-14) কোনো ব্যক্তিকে লক্ষ্য করে গালি দেয়ার ক্ষেত্রে অনেক সময় এই গালির মূল বিষয় নারীকেন্দ্রিক হয়ে থাকে।[\[১৫\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A6-15)[\[১৬\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%AF%E0%A7%8C%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE-16) অর্থাৎ সম্মানহানী করা হয় গালি যাকে দেয়া হচ্ছে তার নিকট কোনো নারী স্বজনের Swearing is a common form of expression in many cultures around the world, and Bengali culture is no exception. In Bengali, swearing can be a way to express strong emotions, frustration, or anger. However, it's important to understand that swearing in Bengali can vary greatly depending on the context and the relationship between the speaker and the listener.

In Bengali culture, there are several ways to swear or use offensive language. One common way is to use words that are considered taboo or vulgar. These words are often used in moments of extreme anger or frustration and are not typically used in polite conversation.

Another way swearing is expressed in Bengali culture is through insults or derogatory terms. These can be directed at someone as a way to insult them or belittle them. It's important to note that using insults in Bengali can be seen as disrespectful and offensive, so it's best to avoid using them unless you're very familiar with the person you're speaking with.

In addition to verbal swearing, gestures and body language can also play a role in expressing strong emotions in Bengali culture. For example, shaking one's head vigorously from side to side can indicate disagreement or disapproval, while raising one's eyebrows can convey surprise or disbelief.

Overall, swearing in Bengali is a complex cultural phenomenon that varies depending on the context and relationship between speakers. While it can be a way to express strong emotions or frustrations, it's important to use caution when using offensive language or gestures as they can be seen as disrespectful or offensive.

In conclusion, swearing in Bengali is an integral part of the culture but should be used with caution and respect for others. Understanding the nuances of swearing in Bengali can help navigate social interactions more effectively and avoid unintentionally causing offense.

কিছু গালি সাধারণভাবে প্রচলিত; আবার কিছু গালি নির্দিষ্ট গোষ্ঠীর সদস্যদের মধ্যে প্রচলিত যা কোনো কোনো ক্ষেত্রে সেই গোষ্ঠীর বৈশিষ্ট্য ফুটিয়ে তোলে। একই ভাষাভাষী মানুষের মধ্যে সংস্কৃতিভেদে গালির উদ্দেশ্য ও ব্যবহার ভিন্ন হতে পারে। গালি যেমন ব্যক্তিকে হেয় করার জন্য প্রয়োগ করা হয়, তেমনি গোষ্ঠীগত অবমাননার উদ্দেশ্যেও গালি প্রদান করা হয়ে থাকে। মানুষ নয় এমন প্রাণী বা বস্তুকেও গালি দেয়া হয়ে থাকে। গালির তীব্রতা বৃদ্ধির জন্য সাধারণ শব্দের পরিবর্তে অশালীন বা অশ্লীল শব্দের প্রয়োগ মানুষের একটি স্বাভাবিক প্রবণতা।[\[১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8-1)[\[২\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC-2)[\[৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%96-3)

গালি আর অকথ্যভাষা অভিন্ন নয়। উদ্দেশ্যের দিক থেকে গালি একধরনের সমালোচনা যা নির্দোষ থেকে আক্রমণাত্মক হতে পারে। গালমন্দ করে মানুষ নিজের ক্ষোভ করে অন্য দিকে ঘৃণাপ্রকাশেল সুখ লাভ করে থাকে।

## ব্যুৎপত্তি

ভাষাবিদ ও অভিধানবিদ বেন জিমার বলেন, "ঐতিহাসিক দিক থেকে গালিকে শনাক্ত করা বেশ কঠিন।"[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4) এর কারণ হিসেবে তিনি বলেন গালি লেখ্যরূপ পাবার অনেক আগে থেকে কথ্যরূপে ব্যবহৃত হয়ে থাকে। এর মধ্যে ঐ শব্দের অর্থ পরিবর্তিত হতে পারে এবং নতুন শব্দ প্রবেশ করতে পারে। এর ফলে গোটা প্রক্রিয়াই জটিল হয়ে পড়ে।[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4) অশ্লীল শব্দার্থে এর ইংরেজি "প্রোফ্যানিটি", যা লাতিন _প্রোফ্যানাস_ ( _profanus_) থেকে এসেছে, যার অর্থ "মন্দিরের পূর্বে (বাইরে)"।[\[৫\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-ProfanityWord-5) এখানে _প্রো_ অর্থ বাইরে আর _ফ্যানাম_ অর্থ মন্দির। প্রোফ্যান বলতে পবিত্রতার অভাব বুঝানো হতো, অন্তত ১৪৫০-এর দিকে। গালি শব্দের অন্যতম (এবং কম নেতিবাচক) ইংরেজি _স্ল্যাং_ শব্দের ব্যবহার দেখতে পাওয়া যায় ১৭৫৬ সালের দিকে। তখন এই শব্দের অর্থ ছিল "নিম্ন" বা "অসম্মানীয়" লোকের ব্যবহৃত শব্দ। উনবিংশ শতকের গোড়ার দিক থেকে স্ল্যাং আর তথাকথিত নিম্নশ্রেণীর লোকের ভাষা হিসেবে সীমাবদ্ধ ছিল না, যদিও এর অর্থগত দিক থেকে ব্যবহার শিক্ষিত বক্তব্যের আওতার বাইরে ছিল।[\[৬\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-oed-6) এই শব্দের ব্যুৎপত্তি নিশ্চিতভাবে জানা যায় না। জোনাথন গ্রিন বলেন, স্ল্যাং শব্দের অর্থ স্ক্যান্ডিনেভিয় শব্দ "স্লেঙ্গেনাম" থেকে আসার সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে, যে শব্দটি _স্লিং_ (ছুঁড়ে দেয়া) শব্দেরও স্রষ্টা। তিনি বলেন স্ল্যাং ছুঁড়ে দেয়া ভাষার অংশ, নিজের বক্তব্য তুলে ধরার দ্রুত ও সৎ উপায়।"[\[৭\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-etymonline-7)[\[৮\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-BriefHistory-8) গ্রিনের মতে প্রাথমিকভাবে গালি ব্যবহৃত হতো অপরাধীদের মধ্যে, তাদের নিজেদের আলোচনা কর্তৃপক্ষের থেকে আড়াল করার জন্য।[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4) বাংলা গালি শব্দটি এসেছে [সংস্কৃত](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%83%E0%A6%A4_%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B7%E0%A6%BE "সংস্কৃত ভাষা") √গাল্ \+ ই-তু. আ. থেকে।

## মনস্তত্ত্ব ও কারণ

হাঁটার পথে হোঁচট খেলে বা ব্যথা পেলে অনেক ক্ষেত্রে সহজাত প্রবৃত্তির মত সহজভাবে অশ্লীল শব্দ বা গালি চলে আসে।[\[১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8-1)[\[৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%96-3) কখনো কখনো নির্দিষ্ট গোষ্ঠীর ব্যবহৃত গালি প্রমাণ করে যে বাকিরা ঐ গোষ্ঠীর বাইরে।[\[৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%82-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82-4)[\[৯\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A3-9) ড. এমা বার্ন তার লেখা _সোয়ারিং ইজ গুড ফর ইউ_ শীর্ষক বইয়ে বলেন, গালি হচ্ছে এমন এক ধরনের ভাষা যা আমরা চমকে গেলে বা স্তম্ভিত হলে বা উৎফুল্ল হলে পরে ব্যবহার করি; অথবা মজা করার জন্য বা কারো প্রতি আক্রমণাত্মক হবার জন্যও ব্যবহার করি। তবে এটা এমন একটা সাংস্কৃতিক ব্যাপার যা কেবল একটি জনগোষ্ঠী, ভাষা, সমাজ, দেশ বা ধর্মের মধ্যেই অর্থপূর্ণ হতে পারে।" অনেক সময়েই বিশেষ সংস্কৃতিতে আপাত নিষিদ্ধ বা ট্যাবু জিনিস থেকে গালি সৃষ্টি হয়। এক্ষেত্রে প্রাণীর নাম, শারীরিক সমস্যাও গালি হিসেবে ব্যবহৃত হয়। অনেক ক্ষেত্রেই এর প্রধান লক্ষ্য মানসিক আঘাত সৃষ্টি করা। কিল বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের মনোবিজ্ঞানের জ্যেষ্ঠ প্রভাষক ড. রিচার্ড স্টিভেন্সের _স্ল্যাং ল্যাবরেটরি_ নামক গবেষণাকেন্দ্রে পরিচালিত গবেষণায় দেখা যায় কিছু ক্ষেত্রে গালি দীর্ঘসময় একই যন্ত্রণা সহ্য করতে সহায়ক হয়। এর কারণ গালির সাথে আবেগের সংযোগ থাকে, আর তার প্রতিক্রিয়া সৃষ্টি হয়। গালি দেয়ার সময় হৃদপিণ্ডের গতিও বেড়ে যায়। মানসিক চাপের মধ্যে বা মানসিকভাবে আঘাতপ্রাপ্ত হওয়ার সময় গালি দিলে এমন প্রতিক্রিয়া সৃষ্টি হতে পারে, যা পূর্বের ব্যথার অনুভূতিকে কিছুটা লাঘব করে দেয়। এই বিশেষ ক্রিয়ার নাম স্ট্রেস-ইন্ডিউউসড অ্যানালজেসিয়া। সংস্কৃতিভেদে গালি অনেক বৈচিত্র্যময় হয়ে থাকে। কখনো পূর্বাপর প্রজন্মকে নির্দেশ করে গালি দেয়া হয়। ম্যান্ডারিন ভাষার কিছু গালি ১৮ প্রজন্মের আগের পূর্বপুরুষকেও সংযুক্ত করে।[\[৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%96-3)

যুক্তরাষ্ট্রভিত্তিক [অ্যাসোসিয়েশন অব সাইকোলজিক্যাল সায়েন্স](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%85%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%A8_%E0%A6%85%E0%A6%AC_%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%87%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2_%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B8?action=edit&redlink=1 "অ্যাসোসিয়েশন অব সাইকোলজিক্যাল সায়েন্স") জার্নালে প্রকাশিত _দ্য ইউটিলিটি অ্যান্ড ইউবিকুইটি অব ট্যাবু ওয়ার্ডস_ শীর্ষক গবেষণাপ্রবন্ধে মনোবিদ টিমোথি জে গালি দেয়াটাকে গাড়ির হর্ন বাজানোর সাথে তুলনা করেন। অন্যের প্রতিক্রিয়া দেখার জন্যও গালির ব্যবহার হতে পারে বলে তিনি মতপ্রকাশ করেন, যেন অন্যের চরিত্রের ভিন্নরূপ আবিষ্কার করা যায়। "রাগ, হতাশা, আনন্দ বা বিস্ময়—এমন আবেগের তীব্রতা বোঝানোর জন্য মানুষ এ ধরনের শব্দ ব্যবহার করে থাকে" বলেও তিনি জানান।[\[১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A8-1)[\[১০\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%9F%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9C%E0%A7%87-10)

## সাহিত্যে গালির ব্যবহার

সাহিত্যে বরাবরই গালির ব্যবহার হয়ে আসছে। [উইলিয়াম শেক্সপিয়ার](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%87%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AE_%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0 "উইলিয়াম শেক্সপিয়ার") তার লেখায় গালির (স্ল্যাং) ব্যবহার করেছেন।[\[১১\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%99%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE-11)

## ভাষাগত লিঙ্গবৈষম্য

ভাষাবিদ ও সমাজতাত্ত্বিকেরা ভাষার মাধ্যমে লিঙ্গবৈষম্যের কথা তুলে ধরেন।[\[১২\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BC%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8-12)[\[১৩\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%95-13) _ডিকশনারি অব আমেরিকান স্ল্যাং_ তৈরির সময় ১৯৭০-এর দশকে ফ্লেক্সনার দেখেন যে "অধিকাংশ মার্কিন গালি তৈরি ও ব্যবহৃত হচ্ছে পুরুষের দ্বারা।"[\[১৪\]](https://bn.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF#cite_note-%E0%A6%AB%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B2%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-14) কোনো ব্যক্তিকে লক্ষ্য করে গালি দেয়ার ক্ষেত্রে অনেক সময় এই গালির মূল বিষয় নারীকেন্দ্রিক হয়ে A description of the king and queen of the termites in Sylheti **Sylheti**[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-9) is an [Indo-Aryan language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Aryan_languages "Indo-Aryan languages") spoken by an estimated 11 million people, primarily in [Sylhet Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_Division "Sylhet Division") of [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh"), [Barak Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barak_Valley "Barak Valley") of [Assam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam "Assam"), and northern parts of [Tripura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripura "Tripura") in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-:0-10)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-eth-11)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-12) In addition, there are substantial numbers of Sylheti speakers in the Indian states of [Meghalaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghalaya "Meghalaya"), [Manipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manipur "Manipur"), and [Nagaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagaland "Nagaland"),[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-eth-11) as well as among [diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diaspora "Diaspora") communities across the globe—from [Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Northern_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland") and [North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") to various parts of the [Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"). It is variously perceived as either a [dialect of Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_dialects "Bengali dialects") or a language in its own right. While many linguists consider it an independent language,[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-mahanta-gope-variety-13)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-khan-lang-14) for many native speakers Sylheti forms the [diglossic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diglossia "Diglossia") [vernacular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernacular "Vernacular"), with [standard Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Bengali "Standard Bengali") forming the [codified lect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codification_(linguistics) "Codification (linguistics)").[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-15) Some incorrectly consider it as a "corrupt" form of Bengali,[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-simmard-corrupt-16) and there is a reported [language shift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_shift "Language shift") from Sylheti to Standard Bengali in Bangladesh, India and the diaspora;[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-simard-shift-17) though Sylheti has more vitality than Standard Bengali among the diaspora in the United Kingdom.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-18) ## Name See also: [Names of Sylhet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Names_of_Sylhet "Names of Sylhet") _Sylheti_ is eponymously named after [Sylhet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet "Sylhet"), referring to the dialect or language spoken of that area.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-19) According to [Grierson (1903)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#CITEREFGrierson1903) the vernacular _was_ called _Sylhettia_ by the Europeans after the town of Sylhet.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-20) Though the speakers at that time referred to it as _Jaintiapuri_, _Purba Srihattiya_, or _Ujania_ with the latter meaning "the language of the upper country".[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-21) Sylheti is also spelt or known as _Sylhetti_ (or _Sileti_), _Sylheti Bangla_ and _Siloti_ (also spelt in _Syloti_ or _Syloty_).[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-22) ## History Sylheti belongs to the Eastern Indo-Aryan languages that evolved from [Magadhi Prakrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magadhi_Prakrit "Magadhi Prakrit").[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-23) The lowlands around Sylhet were originally inhabited by ancient [Khasi people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khasi_people "Khasi people") (Austroasiatic);[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-24) and the earliest known [Indo-Aryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Aryan_peoples "Indo-Aryan peoples") settlements were founded in the 6th century under the Kingdom of [Kamarupa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamarupa "Kamarupa").[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-25)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-26)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-27) The Sylheti language was known as the language of the ancient Surma Valley and the Barak Valley in the sixth century CE, so it is assumed that this language is nearly 15 centuries old. [\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-28) [Sylhet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_town "Sylhet town") (Srihatta) then emerged as a center of lowland territorialism after the 10th century.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-29) The 11th century Bhatera grants from the Srihatta kings Kesavadeva and Isanadeva were written in Sanskrit.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-30)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-31) Another notable copper plate inscription was found in the village of Paschimbhag in [Rajnagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajnagar_Upazila "Rajnagar Upazila"), [Moulvibazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulvibazar_District "Moulvibazar District") that was issued by King [Srichandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Srichandra "Srichandra") during the 10th century.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-32) The Muslim [Conquest of Sylhet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquest_of_Sylhet "Conquest of Sylhet") in 1303 CE extended the migratory movements of Muslims from western lands, who settled among the native population and greatly influenced the local language.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-33) Thus Sylheti derived a large number of words from [Persian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language "Persian language") and [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"),[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-34) indicating the Perso-Arabic influence on the vernacular.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-pak-35) A script was developed in the region called [Sylheti Nagri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_Nagri "Sylheti Nagri"), which primarily focused on disseminating [Sufi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sufism "Sufism") poetry, known as _[puthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puthi "Puthi")_.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-36) Its earliest known work had been written during the 1600s, called _Bhedsar_ by Syed Shah Husayn Alam.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-37) The literature was transcribed in the standard form of late Middle Bengali, it was similar to the _[Dobhashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dobhashi "Dobhashi")_ idiom though phonologically was strongly influenced by Sylheti.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-dHubert-7)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-38) The script was read and taught culturally among households and was not institutionalised,[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-dHubert-7) as the [Islamic dynasties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Persian_culture#Bengal "Indo-Persian culture") who ruled over Bengal established Persian alongside Arabic as the official languages.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-39) Printed texts of the script reached its peak during the late 19th century, however its use became obsolete by around the middle of the 20th century.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-40) In 1903, Grierson reported that Sylheti was spoken only around Sylhet town of the then Sylhet district (now Sylhet Division and Karimganj district in Assam), and that among the Indo-Aryan speakers in the district, about 33 per cent spoke this language.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-41) The earliest appearance of a documentation of Sylheti vocabulary was in the _Government Report on the History and Statistics of Sylhet District_ by T. Walton, B.C.S. in 1857, which contained a list of peculiar words used in Sylhet.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-42) Many terms that were listed here differ from modern Sylheti – highlighting its evolution. In 1868, another short glossary of local terms in various districts of the Dacca Division (which included Sylhet) were written up and compared to standard Bengali to allow ease in understanding local vernaculars.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-heads-43) Despite being annexed to the [Assam Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam_Province "Assam Province") during colonial rule, Sylheti speakers felt a linguistic affinity with the rest of Bengal.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-44) [Bengali literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_literature "Bengali literature") had some influence from Sylheti, popular songwriters or poets such as [Hason Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hason_Raja "Hason Raja") or [Shah Abdul Karim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Abdul_Karim "Shah Abdul Karim"), significantly contributed to the literature.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-45)[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-46) Sylhet was reunited with Bengal following a [referendum in 1947](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_Sylhet_referendum "1947 Sylhet referendum").[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-47) ## Status According to Simard, Dopierala and Thaut, Sylheti is a " [minoritised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minoritized_language "Minoritized language"), politically unrecognised, and understudied language."[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-simard91-lead-48) It is currently not officially recognised as a language in either Bangladesh or India.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-49) Many native speakers consider it to be a _slang_ or corrupt version of Standard Bengali and not an independent language;[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-simmard-corrupt-16) and there is a reported [language shift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_shift "Language shift") to Standard Bengali and a decrease in the number of native speakers since parents are not teaching it to their children.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-simard-shift-17) In Bangladesh, there is a [diglossia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diglossia "Diglossia") where Sylheti is one among other low status [regional dialects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_dialects "Bengali dialects") while Standard Bengali, the [official language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_language "Official language"), has a high status.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-hamid-50) In the Indian state of Assam where [Assamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assamese_language "Assamese language") is the state language, Standard Bengali language serves as an additional official language in its [Barak Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barak_Valley "Barak Valley") districts, which host a majority Sylheti-speaking population.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-51) In the United Kingdom, British schools have begun enlisting Sylheti in their syllabi.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-52) [BBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_News_(British_TV_channel) "BBC News (British TV channel)") has also broadcast online videos relating to [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") in five major [South Asian languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_South_Asia "Languages of South Asia") including Sylheti.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-53) ## Classification ![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Audio-input-microphone.svg/120px-Audio-input-microphone.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail) [Zia Uddin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zia_Uddin's_Voice.ogg "File:Zia Uddin's Voice.ogg") [Zia Uddin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zia_Uddin "Zia Uddin") giving a speech in Sylheti * * * _Problems playing this file? See [media help](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Media "Help:Media")._ [Grierson (1903)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#CITEREFGrierson1903) notes that the language of eastern Sylhet is not intelligible to Bengalis from the west, though he still classed it as Bengali,[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-54) grouping it under "Eastern Bengali".[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-grierson-55) [Chatterji (1926)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#CITEREFChatterji1926) too calls it a dialect of Bengali and places it in the eastern [Vangiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangali_(ethnic_dialect) "Bangali (ethnic dialect)") group of [Magadhi Prakrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magadhi_Prakrit "Magadhi Prakrit") and notes that all Bengali dialects were independent of each other and did not emanate from the literary Bengali called " [sadhu bhasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadhu_bhasha "Sadhu bhasha")".[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-56) Among the different eastern dialect groups, Sylheti and [Chittagonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chittagonian_language "Chittagonian language") have phonetic and morphological properties that are alien to standard Bengali and other western dialects of Bengali,[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChatterji1926[httpsarchiveorgdetailsOriginDevelopmentOfBengaliCHATTERJI_Origin-Development-of-Bengali_Vol-1pagen233mode2upqsylhet_138]-57) and these differences are such that Sylheti is more distant to standard Bengali than is Assamese.[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-58) Recent scholarship notes that these morpho-phonological and [mutual intelligibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutual_intelligibility "Mutual intelligibility") differences are significant enough that Sylheti could claim itself as a language on its own right.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-sen-language-59) [Ethnologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnologue "Ethnologue") groups Sylheti in [Bengali–Assamese languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali%E2%80%93Assamese_languages "Bengali–Assamese languages");[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-e25-5) whereas Glottolog gives further subgrouping and places it in the "Eastern Bengali" group alongside [Hajong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hajong_language "Hajong language"), separately from the Bengali dialects.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-glot-syl-60) ### Language-dialect controversy While modern [sociolinguistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociolinguistics "Sociolinguistics") generally talks about [varieties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(linguistics) "Variety (linguistics)"), rather than languages and dialects, there are still many disagreements about the status of language varieties outside the discipline. These can be for reasons of funding or recognition,[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-61) or for reasons of identity. The classification of Sylheti is contentious—Chalmers (1996) suggested that it was generally identified as a [dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_dialects "Bengali dialects") of [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language") though there were efforts to recognise it as a language.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-rasinger2007-62)[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-63) Grierson had classified Sylheti as an Eastern Bengali dialect and had noted that it "possess all the peculiar characteristics of the extreme Eastern Bengali type."[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-grierson-55) Anecdotal evidence suggests that Sylhetis, who could also speak in Standard Bengali, considered the two languages to be mutually intelligible.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-64)[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-mccarthy2018-mi-65) On the basis of the anecdotal evidence of mutual intelligibility, regionality and the fact that Sylheti is spoken by a predominantly rural community, [Rasinger (2007)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#CITEREFRasinger2007) concludes that Sylheti could be considered a dialect of Bengali.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-66) Simard, Dopierala and Thaut have pointed out that the intelligibility could be an effect of prior exposure of Sylheti speakers to Standard Bengali,[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-67) and that the academic consensus is that mutual intelligibility ranges from "unintelligible" to "hardly intelligible".[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-68) On the basis of phonology and phonetics, lexicon, grammatical structure and a lack of mutual intelligibility, some recent linguists claim that Sylheti is not merely a dialectal variation of Bengali but a language in its own right.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-sen-language-59)[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-simard91-language-69)[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-70) Phonologically Sylheti is distinguished from Standard Bengali and other regional Bengali dialects by significant deaspiration and spirantisation,[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-71) leading to major restructuring of the consonant inventory[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-72) and the development of tones.[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-73) As majority of the diaspora in the United Kingdom speak Sylheti, it created an environment that was somewhat uninfluenced by Standard Bengali, inevitably leading some to view Sylheti as a distinct language.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-74) During the 1980s there were unsuccessful attempts to recognise Sylheti as a language in its own right by a small group in the London Borough of [Tower Hamlets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Borough_of_Tower_Hamlets "London Borough of Tower Hamlets"), which lacked support from the Sylheti community itself.[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-75)[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-76) ## Literature [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d0/Halot-un-nabi-page1.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Halot-un-nabi-page1.gif) Cover of 19th century Halat-un-Nabi by [Sadeq Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadeq_Ali "Sadeq Ali") _Halat-un-Nabi_, a [puthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puthi "Puthi") written by [Sadeq Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadeq_Ali "Sadeq Ali") is considered to be the most prominent literature in Sylheti Nagri.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-syldiv-77) The presence and influence of [Shah Jalal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Jalal "Shah Jalal") and [Shri Chaitanya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shri_Chaitanya "Shri Chaitanya") dev is found in the Sylheti literature.[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-78) According to Syed Mostafa Kamal, (approximately 1650 AD) the [Baul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baul "Baul") tradition was founded based on the combination of Chaitanyavad and Jaganmohani ideologies, that mystic literature influenced and seen in the [Vaishnava Padavali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaishnava_Padavali "Vaishnava Padavali"). As a result, Sylhet is considered as the spiritual capital of mysticism and the fertile land of Baul music.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-syldiv-77) A great number of poets enriched Sylheti literature. Among them, [Hason Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hason_Raja "Hason Raja"), [Radha Raman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radharaman_Dutta "Radharaman Dutta"), Syed Shah Noor, Shitalong Shaha, Durbin Shaha are noteworthy. The main theme of the Nagri literature are mainly religious, [Islamic history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_history "Islamic history"), tradition, stories, Raga, Baul and mystic music. There have been 140 books found, including 88 printed books in Sylheti Nagri script.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-sylgov-79) ## Writing system Main article: [Sylheti Nagri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_Nagri "Sylheti Nagri") Sylheti currently does not have a standardised writing system.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-GESIS-80) Historically in the Sylhet region, the [Sylheti Nagri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_Nagri "Sylheti Nagri") script was used alongside the Bengali script.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-dHubert-7) Sylheti Nagri was however mostly limited to writing religious poetry.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-grierson-55) The script often avoided [tatsama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatsama "Tatsama") (Sanskrit-derived terms) and incorporated Perso-Arabic vocabulary. Additionally, Sylheti Nagri texts were traditionally paginated from right to left.[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-81)[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-82) It is claimed by some that the orthography of the script equates with Sylheti, due to the fewer characters compared with the Bengali script as there are fewer phonemes found in Sylheti.[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-83) An endangered script, it has since seen a revival mostly by academics and linguists.[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-84) Because [Standard Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Bengali "Standard Bengali") is the [medium of instruction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium_of_instruction "Medium of instruction") of state schools in Bangladesh,[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-85) some may write Sylheti using the [Bengali–Assamese script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali%E2%80%93Assamese_script "Bengali–Assamese script").[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-GESIS-80) In United Kingdom, publishers use [Latin script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_script "Latin script") for Sylheti and according to the Sylheti Translation and Research (STAR), Latin (Roman) script is the most _used_ script for writing Sylheti.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-STAR-86) The [New Testament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Testament "New Testament") in Sylheti was published in the [Sylhet Nagri script](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_Nagri "Sylheti Nagri") along with versions in the Latin and in the Bengali–Assamese script, in 2014.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-87) STAR is developing a (three script) transliteration system As of 2025[\[update\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sylheti_language&action=edit), transliterating the language's name, for example as _Siloṭi_ in Latin script.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-STAR-86) ## Geographical distribution [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Brick_Lane_Banglatown.jpg/960px-Brick_Lane_Banglatown.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brick_Lane_Banglatown.jpg) _Banglatown_ in Brick Lane, London, UK, which is home to one of the largest Sylheti diaspora communities in the western world[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Sylhetis_in_Bangladesh.png/500px-Sylhetis_in_Bangladesh.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sylhetis_in_Bangladesh.png) A map showing the distribution of Sylheti speakers in Bangladesh. Sylheti is the primary language of the [Sylhet Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_Division "Sylhet Division") in north-eastern Bangladesh, with its concentration mostly in the districts of [Sylhet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_District "Sylhet District"), [Moulvibazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulvibazar_District "Moulvibazar District"), _eastern_ [Sunamganj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunamganj_District "Sunamganj District") and _north-eastern_ [Habiganj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habiganj_District "Habiganj District").[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-ReferenceA-88) Recent findings assert that the local dialect spoken in much of the Habiganj district differs quite significantly from Sylheti.[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-89) According to dialectal studies, the dialects spoken in [Habiganj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habiganj_district "Habiganj district") and [Sunamganj districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunamganj_district "Sunamganj district") are phonologically and grammatically more similar to [Brahmanbaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahmanbaria_district "Brahmanbaria district") and [East Mymensingh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netrokona_district "Netrokona district") than eastern parts of [Sylhet division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylhet_division "Sylhet division"). Therefore, the dialect of western Sylhet (Habiganj-Sunamganj) is classified with the dialects of [Greater Dhaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka_division "Dhaka division"), [Mymensingh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mymensingh_division "Mymensingh division"), [Comilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghna_Division "Meghna Division") etc. regions by scholars as it is dialectally allied with these regions.[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-90)[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-91) Sylheti is also widely spoken in the southern [Assam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam "Assam") region of [Barak Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barak_Valley "Barak Valley"), India, which includes the districts of [Cachar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cachar_district "Cachar district"), [Hailakandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hailakandi_district "Hailakandi district") and [Karimganj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karimganj_District "Karimganj District").[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-92) In addition, it is spoken in the northern parts of [Tripura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripura "Tripura")[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-:0-10)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-eth-11) and [Jiribam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiribam_district "Jiribam district"), Manipur.[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-ReferenceA-88) There is also a significant population of Sylheti speakers in [Hojai district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hojai_district "Hojai district") of Central Assam,[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-ReferenceA-88) [Shillong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shillong "Shillong") in Meghalaya,[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-93) and the state of [Nagaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagaland "Nagaland").[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-eth-11) A few numbers are also located in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), most of whom are migrants from Assam. Outside the [Indian subcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent "Indian subcontinent"), the largest grouping of Sylheti speakers reside in the United Kingdom, of which 95 per cent of [British Bangladeshis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Bangladeshi "British Bangladeshi") have origins from the Sylhet region.[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-94) It is estimated there are around 400,000 Sylheti speakers in the UK.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-GESIS-80) The largest concentration live in [east London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_London "East London") boroughs, such as Tower Hamlets.[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-Guardian-95) There are also significant numbers of speakers in the United States, most are concentrated in New York City,[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-96) and in [Hamtramck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamtramck,_Michigan "Hamtramck, Michigan"), Michigan where majority of [Bangladeshi Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladeshi_Americans "Bangladeshi Americans") there are of Sylheti origin.[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-97)[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-98) There are also small numbers located in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Canada.[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-99)[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-100) Significant Sylheti-speaking communities reside in the [Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladeshis_in_the_Middle_East "Bangladeshis in the Middle East") of which most are migrant workers,[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-101)[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-102) and in many other countries throughout the world. ## Lexicon Sylheti shares most linguistic properties with Standard Bengali,[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-103)\[ _[bettersourceneeded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_\] with a [lexical similarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexical_similarity "Lexical similarity") of 70%.[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-104)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-eth-11) ## Phonology The phoneme inventory of Sylheti differs from both [Standard Rarhi Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language") as well as the [typical Bangladeshi Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bengali "Eastern Bengali").[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-105) It is characterised by a loss of breathiness and aspiration contrasts, leading to a significant reduction in its phoneme inventory and to the [development of tones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tone_(linguistics) "Tone (linguistics)"). In particular, the following developments are seen:[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-mg18-phoneme-inventory-106)[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-107) - Both voiced and voiceless aspirated stops have become unaspirated (d̪ʱ → d̪; t̪ʰ → t̪). - The voiceless labials have spirantised to homorganic fricatives (p → ɸ; pʰ → ɸ). - The velar stops have become velar fricatives (k → x; kʰ → x), although \[k\] can be heard as an allophone of /x/ when preceded by high vowels /i,u/. - The post-alveolar affricates have spirantised to alveolar fricatives (tʃ → s; tʃʰ → s; dʒ → z; dʒʱ → z). - Among the voiceless stops only the dental /t̪, d̪/ and retroflex /ʈ, ɖ/ stops have remained stops. For example, when the suffix - _ṭain_ (the inanimate plural marker) is added to a nominal, it will take the opposite tone of the root: _bari-ṭáin_ (from _bari_ "home") vs. _bárí-ṭain_ (from _bárí_ "heavy"). A more recent study shows that there is a three-way tonal system in Sylheti words with two syllables or more. According to this analysis, words with aspiration in the final syllable historically gain a high tone across the word, whilst those with initial aspiration have this replaced by a low tone across the word. Sylheti continues to have a long history of coexisting with tonal [Tibeto-Burman languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibeto-Burman_languages "Tibeto-Burman languages") including various dialects of [Kokborok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kokborok "Kokborok") such as [Reang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reang "Reang"). on/ in the shoes | Noun Inflection Note how the case endings attach after the measure word. For the genitive case, the ending may change depending on the last phoneme of the noun. A noun (without an article) which ends either in a consonant or in the inherent vowel, ꠅ _o_, is inflected by adding –ꠞ - _or_ to the end of the word (and deleting the inherent vowel if applicable). An example of this would be the genitive of ꠉꠥꠍ _gus_ 'meat' being ꠉꠥꠍ **ꠞ** _gus **or**_ 'of meat' or '(the) meat's'. A noun which ends in any vowel apart from the inherent vowel will just have a -ꠞ - _r_ following it, as in the genitive of ꠙꠥꠀ _fua_ being ꠙꠥꠀ **ꠞ** _fua **r**_ '(the) boy's'. The genitive ending is also applied to verbs (in their verbal noun forms), which is most commonly seen when using postpositions (for example: ꠢꠤꠇꠘ **ꠞ** ꠟꠣꠉꠤ _hiknor_ _lagi_, 'for learning'). For the locative case, only applicable to inanimate nouns, the case marker also changes in a similar fashion to the genitive case, with consonants and the inherent vowel having their own ending, -ꠅ - _o_, and all other vowels having another ending, -ꠔ - _t_. For example, ꠍꠤꠟꠐ **ꠅ** _siloṭ **o**_ 'in Sylhet', ꠑꠣꠇꠣ **ꠔ** _ḍáxát_ 'in Dhaka'. ##### Marked nominative / Ergative The subject of a [transitive verb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transitive_verb "Transitive verb") in Sylheti is marked with the case marker - ꠦ _-e_ after consonant endings, and -ꠄ _-e_ after vowel endings and after the generic definite article ending -ꠔꠣ - _ta_.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-Das2017-114) Thus: ꠙꠥꠘꠝꠦ Punom- **e** Punom-NOM ꠜꠣꠔ bát rice ꠈꠞ xár eat-PRES.CONT. ꠙꠥꠘꠝꠦꠜꠣꠔꠈꠞ Punom- **e** bát xár Punom-NOM rice eat-PRES.CONT. Punom is eating rice. On the other hand, the subject of an intransitive verb, or of the verb ꠎꠣꠃꠣ _zaua_ 'to go', takes no case marker in its nominative case.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-Das2017-114) ꠝꠤꠘꠣ Mina Mina-(NOM) ꠈꠥꠛ xúb very ꠌꠣꠟꠣꠇ salax clever ꠝꠤꠘꠣꠈꠥꠛꠌꠣꠟꠣꠇ Mina xúb salax Mina-(NOM) very clever Mina is very clever. This feature of Sylheti is closer to [Assamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assamese_language "Assamese language") than to Standard Bengali. This marked nominative case has been called an [ergative case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ergative_case "Ergative case"), and has also led to Sylheti being classified as an [ergative–absolutive language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ergative%E2%80%93absolutive_alignment "Ergative–absolutive alignment"). The particular system of [split ergativity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split_ergativity "Split ergativity") that Sylheti uses appears to be a retention of the system that emerged from [Magadhi Prakrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magadhi_Prakrit "Magadhi Prakrit").[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-Saikia2022-115) However, in Sylheti, this marked nominative is only exhibited by nouns, and not by pronouns.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylheti_language#cite_note-Das2017-114) #### Measure words When counted, nouns must also be accompanied by the appropriate [measure word](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measure_word "Measure word"). The noun's measure word ( **MW**) must be used in between the numeral and the noun. Most nouns take the generic measure word _gu/ṭa/xán_, although there are many more specific measure words, such as _zon_, which is only used to count humans. | Sylheti | | Noy- **ṭa**

However, omitting the noun and preserving the measure word is grammatical and not uncommon to hear. For example, _Xáli êx- **zon** táxbo._ (lit. 'Only one- **MW** will remain.') would be understood to mean 'Only one **person** will remain.', since _zon_ can only be used to count humans. ### Pronouns #### Personal pronouns Sylheti personal pronouns are somewhat similar to English pronouns, having different words for first, second, and third person, and also for singular and plural (unlike for verbs, below). Sylheti pronouns, like their English counterparts, do differentiate for gender. Sylheti has different third-person pronouns for proximity. The first are used for someone who is nearby, and the second are for those who are a little further away. The third are usually for those who are not present. In addition, each of the second- and third-person pronouns have different forms for the familiar and polite forms; the second person also has a "very familiar" form (sometimes called "despective"). It may be noted that the "very familiar" form is used when addressing particularly close friends or family as well as for addressing subordinates, or in abusive language. Some adjectives form their opposites by prefixing ꠛꠦ- _be-_, or sometimes ꠘꠤ- _ni-_; for example, the opposite of ꠞꠥꠎꠉꠣꠞ ( _ruzgar_, 'earning') is ꠛꠦꠞꠥꠎꠉꠣꠞ ( _beruzgar_, 'not earning, idle, mendicant'), the opposite of ꠇꠣꠝꠣ ( _xama_, 'of use') is ꠘꠤꠇꠣꠝꠣ ( _nixama_, 'useless, of no use'). Demonstrative adjectives – 'this' and 'that' – correspond to ꠁ, ꠅ/ꠅꠃ _i, o/ou_ and ꠢꠤ, ꠢ/ꠢꠃ _hi, ho/hou_, with the definite article attached to the following noun. Thus, 'this book' would translate to ꠁ/ꠅꠃ ꠛꠁꠈꠣꠘ _i boi-xan_, while 'those books' would translate to ꠢꠃ ꠛꠁ-ꠉꠤꠍꠤꠘ/ꠛꠁ-ꠉꠥꠘ/ꠛꠁ-ꠀꠁꠘ _hi boi-gisin/boi-gun/boi-ain_. #### Comparatives and superlatives Sylheti adjectives form their comparative forms with ꠀꠞꠅ ( _aro_, 'more'), and their superlative forms with ꠡꠛ ꠕꠣꠇꠤ ( _shob táki_, 'than all'). Comparisons are formed by using genitive form of the object of comparison, followed by the postposition ꠕꠣꠇꠤ/ꠕꠘꠤ ( _táki/tóni_, 'than') or the postposition ꠟꠣꠇꠣꠘ ( _laxan_, 'like') and then by ꠀꠞꠅ ( _aro_, 'more') or ꠇꠝ ( _xom_, 'less'). The word for 'more' is optional, but the word for 'less' is required, so in its absence 'more' is inferred. Adjectives can be additionally modified by using ꠛꠟꠘ/ꠛꠣꠇ꠆ꠇꠣ/ꠛꠃꠔ ( _bolon/bakka/bout_, 'much') or ꠛꠃꠔ ( _bout_, 'much'), which are especially useful for comparing quantities. | Sylheti | Literal Translation | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | ꠇꠞꠤꠝ ꠞꠢꠤꠝꠞ ꠕꠘꠤ ꠟꠣꠝ꠆ꠙꠣ
